skills-first: skills-first is a term used to describe a new approach to talent management that emphasizes a person’s skills and competencies – rather than degrees, job histories or job titles – with regard to attracting, hiring, developing, and redeploying talent.
TAE Sector: The TAE sector stands for "Training and Adult Education" sector. It encompasses organizations, institutions, and initiatives involved in providing training, education, and professional development opportunities for adults, with a focus on enhancing skills, knowledge, and competencies for career advancement and personal growth. The TAE sector comprises training institutions and adult education professionals.
Low Wage Worker: Referencing MOM's definition, lower-wage workers refers to full-time resident employees earnign a gross monthly income from work (excluding employer Central Provident Fund (CPF) contribitions) up to and including the 20th percentile income level of full-time employed residents (excluding employer CPF contributions), which was $2492 in Jun 2022.
PWDs:
Refers to Persons with Disabilities. PWDs are defined as individuals with physical, sensory, intellectual and/or development impairments which substanitally reduce their prospects of securing and retaining hobs, advancing in education and training, employment and recreation. 
(Refer to : www.sgenable.sg/about-us/our-impact/disability-in-singapore for more information)
platform workers:
Referencing the definition by the Advisory Commitee on Platform Workers set up by Ministry of Manpower in 2021, platform workers refers to delivery workers, private-hire car drivers and taxi drivers who use online platforms to match them with demand for their delivery and point-to-point transport services, but who are not employees of the companies operating these platforms. 
(Refer to https://www.mom.gov.sg/newsroom/press-releases/2022/government-accepts-recommendations-by-the-advisory-committee-on-platform-workers for more information)
Gig Workers:
In general, the terms refers to own account workers or Self-employed persons (SEPs) who operate their own business without hiring any employees and who source for a significant part of their work through online matching platforms. 
(Reference: MOM's PQ reply www.mom.gov.sg/newsroom/parliament-questions-and-replies/2021/0202-written-answer-by-mrs-josephine-teo-minister-for-manpower-to-pq-on-breakdown-of-gig-workers)
Self-Employed Worker: Self-employed workers perform work for others (e.g. provide a service) under a contract for service. Generally, sole-proprietors and partners registered with the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA) are self-employed.
Non-University Graduates: In Singapore, non-university graduates refer to individuals who have not obtained a degree from a university. This group may include individuals with diplomas, vocational qualifications, or other forms of post-secondary education, as well as those who have completed their education at the secondary level.
Fresh Graduates: Fresh graduates in Singapore refer to individuals who have recently completed their tertiary education, typically at the diploma or degree level, and are entering the workforce for the first time. These individuals have limited or no prior full-time work experience in their respective fields of study.
SMEs: In Singapore, SMEs (Small and Medium-sized Enterprises) are defined as companies with annual sales turnover of not more than S$100 million, or employing no more than 200 workers.
LLEs: Large Local Enterprises (LLEs) in Singapore typically refer to locally-owned companies that have substantial operations and a significant presence in the domestic market. These enterprises often have a considerable workforce and play a significant role in the country's economy, contributing to employment, innovation, and industry development.
MNCs: In Singapore, MNCs (Multinational Corporations) are companies that have operations and business activities in multiple countries, including Singapore. These corporations often have a global presence, with headquarters or significant operations in different parts of the world, and they play a crucial role in the country's economy, contributing to employment, investment, and international trade.
Adult Educators: Adult educators are professionals who specialize in teaching and facilitating learning experiences for adult learners. They possess expertise in adult learning principles, instructional design, and the delivery of educational programs tailored to the needs and characteristics of adult students. These educators may work in various settings, including vocational training institutions, adult education centers, corporate training departments, and community-based learning organizations.
Training Providers: Training providers are organizations or institutions that offer educational and skills development programs to individuals and professionals. These providers deliver a wide range of training courses, workshops, and certification programs aimed at enhancing the knowledge, competencies, and capabilities of participants in various fields such as vocational skills, professional development, and industry-specific training. Training providers may include educational institutions, private training organizations, industry associations, and government agencies involved in workforce development.
Workplace Learning: Workplace learning refers to the process of acquiring knowledge, skills, and competencies within the context of one's job or professional environment. It involves formal, informal or non-formal learning activities that take place on the job, such as on-the-job training, mentorship, job rotations, and other experiential learning opportunities aimed at enhancing an individual's performance, productivity, and adaptability within the workplace.
Digitalization: Digitalisation refers to the process of integrating digital technologies, tools, and practices into various aspects of an organization, industry, or society to enhance efficiency, productivity, and innovation. It involves the adoption of digital solutions, automation, data analytics, and the transformation of traditional processes and services into digital formats to improve operations, decision-making, and customer experiences. In the context of learning or education, digitalisation involves the integration of digital tecjnologies and tools into the process of education and training. This includes the use of digital platforms, online resources, interactive content, and virtual learning environments to deliver and enhance learning experiences. Digitalisation of learning aims to leverage technology to make education more accessible, interactive, and adaptable to the needs of learners, while also enabling data-driven insights and personalized learning approaches.
Individual Agency: Individual agency refers to an individual's capacity and autonomy to make choices, take actions, and exert control over their own lives. It encompasses the ability to set goals, make decisions, and act upon them, often in pursuit of personal and professional development.
Motivation: Motivation, on the other hand, refers to the internal and external factors that drive an individual's behavior, actions, and efforts towards achieving specific goals or outcomes. It involves the energization, direction, and persistence of one's efforts towards a desired objective, often influenced by personal aspirations, needs, and external incentives.
Skills Training: In Singapore, skills training refers to structured educational programs and initiatives designed to develop and enhance the technical, vocational, and professional competencies of individuals. These training programs are aimed at equipping participants with the specific skills, knowledge, and capabilities required to excel in various industries and occupations, contributing to their employability, career advancement, and overall productivity. Skills training in Singapore is often aligned with industry needs and may be offered by educational institutions, training providers, and government-supported initiatives.
Pedagogy: Pedagogy refers to the theory and practice of teaching and educating children. It encompasses the methods, strategies, and principles used by educators to facilitate learning and development in young learners, typically in formal educational settings such as schools and early childhood education centers.
Andragogy: Andragogy, on the other hand, is the theory and practice of teaching and educating adult learners. It focuses on the specific characteristics, motivations, and learning needs of adult learners, emphasizing self-directed learning, practical application of knowledge, and the relevance of learning to adult life and work experiences. Andragogy is often associated with adult education, professional development, and lifelong learning initiatives.
Science of Learning: The science of adult learning in Singapore encompasses the study and application of principles, theories, and methodologies related to how adults learn and develop knowledge, skills, and competencies. It involves understanding the unique characteristics, motivations, and learning styles of adult learners, as well as designing and delivering effective educational programs and interventions tailored to the needs of adult learners in various contexts, including vocational training, professional development, and lifelong learning initiatives.
Communities of Practice:
The concept of communities of practice was pioneered by Jean Lave and Etienne Wenger in their work on situated learning and communities of practice. Their research emphasized the importance of social learning and the development of identity and expertise within communities of practice, contributing to a deeper understanding of how individuals learn and collaborate within professional and social contexts.

In current context, communities of practice are groups of people who share a concern, a set of problems, or a passion about a topic, and who deepen their knowledge and expertise in this area by interacting on an ongoing basis. These communities can take many forms, from informal networks to formalized groups, and they serve as environments for learning, sharing experiences, and developing best practices within a specific domain or field of interest.
Critical Core Skills:
Critical Core Skills (CCS) comprises 16 competencies across three skills cluster, that workplaces deem essential. They are:

Thinking Critically: Cognitive skills are the root of technical skill development and progression. It is needed to think broadly and creatively to see connections and opportunities during change.

Interacting with Others: Learning from others is an effective way to acquire new skills, exchange ideas and build a shared understanding of a problem or situation.

Staying Relevant: Managing oneself effectively and paying close attention to trends that impact work and living, to provide the strategies, direction and motivation for technical skill development.

(https://www.skillsfuture.gov.sg/initiatives/mid-career/criticalcoreskills)
Blended Learning: Blended learning is an instructional approach that combines traditional face-to-face classroom teaching with online digital resources and activities. It involves a strategic integration of in-person interactions, such as lectures, discussions, or workshops, with digital learning components, including online modules, multimedia resources, and interactive exercises. Blended learning aims to leverage the strengths of both traditional and digital learning methods to create a comprehensive and flexible learning experience.
